answer: Give every identity sole custodianship of one unique slice of a shared index for an epoch, like a falcon holding a dawn watch nobody else can cover. Entries arrive unpredictably all epoch, and the custodian must publish incremental, signed updates as each new entry lands, so the slice's trail is continuous work, not a precomputable answer. A sybil operator running many identities must service many slices concurrently, each demanding distinct live updates; slices serviced in echo of one another, or left stale, expose the cluster, and abandoned slices lose standing.
